Rune’s Radar

Ask what they want to do first: fitness, games, social experiences, productivity, or mixed reality. Then narrow the choice using fit, storage, performance expectations, and budget.

Lead with one real moment: taking a first-person photo, listening without earbuds, making a call, or asking Meta AI for hands-free help. Note that features can vary by region, language, and account.

Pick one task the customer already cares about, demonstrate it end to end, then explain what the assistant used and what the customer controls. Keep availability caveats clear and specific.

When a new product appears, identify its real category first: camera and audio glasses, display glasses, or immersive headsets. Then compare field of view, input method, battery expectations, and whether it is announced or shipping.

The useful question is no longer whether mixed reality works once. Look for apps people return to, reliable room setup, comfortable input, and clear reasons to blend digital content with the physical space.

Standalone prioritizes quick setup and freedom of movement. PC VR can trade convenience for higher-end rendering and a different library. Industry coverage should name that trade-off instead of treating every headset as interchangeable.
